title: Connection Before Control
shortDefinition: You must attach the correct body points before trying to hold or steer the opponent.
whyItMatters: Without connection, pressure is just strength; the opponent rotates, frames, or exits angle.
deepExplanation: Connection is chest-to-back, chest-to-hip, elbow-knee, head-to-ribs, or grip-to-hip. It sends force through structure and weight instead of biceps.
beginnerView: Touch the right point before squeezing or pulling.
advancedView: Change connection as phases change: passing, pinning, submissions, and retention use different anchors.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Connection Before Control during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Connection Before Control to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Connection Before Control is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Connection Before Control before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
